issue.title: chore: Fix user reports emitting invalid NIP-56 e tags
issue.body:
## Description

User reports could publish invalid NIP-56 `e` tags when there was no related event.
That happened because the local synthetic target `user_<pubkey>` was also being sent as an event tag.
This change keeps that synthetic target for local report history, but only sends real 64-character hex event ids as NIP-56 `e` tags.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4420

## Out of Scope

None.
This is limited to fixing the report event tags while preserving the existing report flow and local history behavior.

## Verification

I rebased onto the latest `origin/main` and ran the repo checks from `mobile/`.
The full Flutter test suite passed.

- `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`
- `mise exec -- dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test integration_test`
- `mise exec -- flutter analyze lib test integration_test`
- `mise exec -- flutter test`

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

review.body:
## Review summary

Localization fix is well-conceived — switching to `_localizedActorSentenceSpans(fullText: l10n.notificationXxx(actor), actorName: actor)` is the right design because it locates the actor span within the *localized* sentence, so word orders like Filipino's `"Sinimulan kang i-follow ni {actorName}"` (actor at end) render the bold span correctly. Verified against all 18 ARB files.

Goldens look correct. The two new layout-invariant tests ("Follow-back button shares its row with the avatar so message text width is stable" / "timestamp moves to the quote when commentText is present") pin non-obvious rendering contracts that would silently regress otherwise.

Scope statement in the PR body is honest — only the row variants are addressed for #3387; the rest of the max-font audit and the device QA matrix in #4387 remain open. Consider adding `Closes #4206` to the body so it auto-closes on merge (#3387 / #4387 are correctly left non-closing).

Inline comments below cover the issues worth addressing in this PR vs. as follow-ups. None are blocking; #1, #4, and #6 are cheap fixes I'd do in this PR rather than later.

comment.body: **[nit]** Centralizing `MockPathProviderPlatform` here is good, but three pre-existing local copies remain in `clip_editor_bloc_test.dart`, `upload_initialization_helper_test.dart`, `upload_manager_sandbox_test.dart`. Out of scope for this PR but a 5-minute follow-up to delete those once they switch to `setupTestEnvironment()`.

**[nit]** Threshold-edge coverage missing. This test uses scale=2 (well above) and other tests use scale=1 (well below) — but no test confirms scale=1.34 stays inline and scale=1.36 stacks. A parametric pair would lock the threshold itself and surface accidental changes to `1.35`.

**[nit]** This is the first place in the repo using a tolerant golden comparator. The 3% tolerance is justified (Linux CI antialiasing drift) and the comparator is scoped to a single test file, so the precedent is contained — but worth calling out in the PR description so future devs don't copy-paste it onto unrelated goldens where a real layout regression should fail loudly.
**[should-fix #4 — rules violation, paired]** Same hardcoded `'Follow back'` as line 57 — see that comment for the fix.

**[should-fix #4 — rules violation]** `rules/localization.md` forbids hardcoded English in widget test assertions:

> Never hardcode English strings in widget test assertions — resolve the key from `AppLocalizations` instead, so the test survives copy changes and breaks loudly if the widget stops reading from l10n.

This file already imports `AppLocalizations`; one-line fix:

```dart
final l10n = lookupAppLocalizations(const Locale('en'));
expect(find.text(l10n.notificationFollowBack), findsOneWidget);
```

(`actor_notification_row_test.dart` already uses `_l10n.notificationFollowBack` correctly — this golden test just missed the convention.)

Same applies at line 88 below.

**[nit]** `zh` is a dead branch — Chinese is not in `AppLocalizations.supportedLocales` (the 18 supported are am, ar, bg, de, en, es, fil, fr, id, it, ja, ko, nl, pl, pt, ro, sv, tr). Either drop `zh` or leave a `// Anticipates zh when added — currently unreachable.` comment.

comment.body:
**[should-fix #3]** `notificationRepliedToYourComment` is the only actor-bearing notification key without an `{actorName}` placeholder — every sibling (`notificationStartedFollowing`, `notificationMentionedYou`, `notificationLikedYourVideo`, …) is parameterized. That forces this PR to add `_replyMessage` + `_usesTightActorJoin` + `_replyActorName` and special-case Japanese `さん` *in code*, while Korean translators handled the same problem by baking `님이` directly into the verb string (`"님이 회원님의 댓글에 답글을 남겼습니다"`). So the Korean honorific lives in data and the Japanese honorific lives in code — that asymmetry will bite a future translator.

Clean fix: parameterize the key for all 18 locales (`"{actorName} replied to your comment"` in en, translators position the placeholder per their language) and then `reply` joins the same `_localizedActorSentenceSpans` codepath as the other kinds. All three helpers delete.

If out of scope here, add a `// TODO(#issue):` per `rules/code_style.md` so the special-case helpers don't become permanent.

**[should-fix #2]** `_localizedActorSentenceSpans` is identical to the one at `actor_notification_row.dart:263` — ~25 lines duplicated verbatim. Extract to a shared helper in `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/notification_actor_spans.dart` and import from both rows. `_messageFor` should stay per-file (different `NotificationKind` cases), but the span-splitting primitive should not.

**[nit]** `showInlineThumbnail` is confusing. Its `true` value means "stack the thumbnail INSIDE the content column" (i.e. NOT inline in the main row). "Inline" reads either way here. Rename to `showStackedThumbnail` or `embedThumbnailInContent` to disambiguate.

**[should-fix #1, paired]** Same `1.35` threshold as `actor_notification_row.dart:102`. Pull both to `NotificationConstants.largeTextStackThreshold` so the two rows stack in sync.

Also worth noting: this is text-scale-only. The actual failure mode (clipping, overflow) is a function of text scale **and** available width. On a 320-wide narrow viewport (split-screen, side-rail tablet layout) the row can still overflow at scale=1.0. A `LayoutBuilder`-based decision (`shouldStack = textScale > 1.35 || maxWidth < W`) is more robust — reasonable follow-up, not strictly blocking.

**[should-fix #1]** Magic threshold `1.35` is duplicated here and at `video_notification_row.dart:47`. This is a layout contract — both rows must stack at the same threshold or the inbox gets inconsistent breakpoints across notification kinds. Extract to `NotificationConstants` (file already imported above):

```dart
static const double largeTextStackThreshold = 1.35;
```

And add a one-line justification (e.g. "Empirical threshold where the 56×56 thumbnail / 32×32 Follow-back button starts forcing message text to clip on a 320-wide row").

issue.title: DM: surface swallowed DAO bookkeeping failures in self-wrap recovery paths
issue.body:
## Summary

`DmRepository.recoverSelfWrap` and `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` swallow DAO bookkeeping failures via `Log.error` only. Crashlytics doesn't see them because the wrapped errors are not `Reportable` per `.claude/rules/error_handling.md`. Today we have no signal for how often these doubly-degraded paths fire in production.

## Problem

The doubly-degraded path in `recoverSelfWrap` (publish landed; both `deleteById` and fallback `markSelfWrapStatus(sent)` threw) is documented as safe via NIP-17 receive-side dedup — but "safe" is hypothesis until we measure. Same for any DAO write failure inside the recipient-success finalize path. We currently have no way to know if this is happening 0/day or 100/day.

## Desired Outcome

Surface DAO bookkeeping failures in these recovery paths so they're visible in monitoring without flooding Crashlytics.

## Scope

Decide between:

1. **Wrap as `Reportable`** per the matrix in `.claude/rules/error_handling.md`. These are arguably "programming-invariant violations" once the publish has landed — the row should always be writeable. Risk: Crashlytics noise on transient SQLite contention.
2. **Counter / debug surface only.** Increment a metric, expose under a debug screen. Less noisy, but invisible without proactive checking.
3. **Both.** Counter for triage, `Reportable` only on persistent runs (e.g., N consecutive failures for the same rumor).

## Context

- Two specific call sites today, both in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart`: `recoverSelfWrap` doubly-degraded catch, plus any throw inside `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` (currently upstream of any try/catch on the caller side).
- Spotted during PR #4106 review by Liz; follow-up to #4102.

issue.title: Fix user reports emitting invalid NIP-56 e tags
issue.body:
## Problem

Mobile user-report events can emit invalid NIP-56 report targets.

`ContentReportingService.reportUser()` falls back to a synthetic event id when no related event is provided:

```dart
final eventId = (relatedEventIds != null && relatedEventIds.isNotEmpty)
    ? relatedEventIds.first
    : 'user_$userPubkey';
```

That value is then used as the NIP-56 `e` tag in `_createReportingEvent()`:

```dart
['e', eventId, nip56Type],
['p', authorPubkey, nip56Type],
```

For DM user reports, `ConversationActionsCubit.reportUser()` calls `reportUser()` without `relatedEventIds`, producing kind `1984` events like:

```text
e tag: user_<64-char-pubkey>
p tag: <64-char-pubkey>
```

This is not a valid event id. Funnelcake currently aggregates report events through `report_counts_mv`, which expects `e` tag targets to be 64-char event ids. In production, ClickHouse has stored kind `1984` report events with invalid `e` targets matching this mobile format, for example:

```text
user_e680e1c186eb8d618dbd5db1e18ec4b84fdd79fddb3987692f640a33a09cf3db
```

Those malformed report events can cause Funnelcake insert failures when `report_counts_mv` tries to write the target into `FixedString(64)`.

## Scope

Update mobile user-report event construction so user reports do not place `user_<pubkey>` in a NIP-56 `e` tag.

Suggested behavior:

- For user reports with no related event id, use the `p` tag as the target and omit the `e` tag.
- For user reports with one or more real related event ids, include valid `e` tags only for actual 64-char event ids.
- Preserve the `p` tag with the reported user's pubkey and the NIP-56 report type.
- Preserve existing local report history and user-facing report flow behavior.

## Relevant Code

- `mobile/lib/services/content_reporting_service.dart`
- `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/conversation_actions/conversation_actions_cubit.dart`
- Related dialog path: `mobile/lib/widgets/report_content_dialog.dart`

## Test Plan

- Add or update unit tests for `ContentReportingService.reportUser()` with no `relatedEventIds`.
- Assert the produced kind `1984` event does not contain an `e` tag with `user_<pubkey>`.
- Assert the produced event includes a `p` tag for the reported user pubkey with the report type.
- Add/update tests for `reportUser()` with valid related event ids and assert only valid event ids are emitted as `e` tags.
- Add/update tests for DM conversation user reporting to cover the no-related-event path.
- Manually verify reporting a DM user still succeeds from the UI.

## Dependency / Coordination Notes

Funnelcake should also defensively filter `report_counts_mv` to ignore malformed `e` targets, because relays should not rely on all clients being well-formed. This mobile issue fixes the known client-side producer of `user_<pubkey>` `e` tags.

issue.title: DM: add recoverFullSend primitive for recipient-wrap-failed outgoing_dms rows
issue.body:
## Summary

`outgoing_dms` rows can land in `recipient_wrap_status: failed / self_wrap_status: failed` state when the recipient gift-wrap publish itself fails (set by `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure` in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart`). Today there is no recovery primitive for this state — only `recoverSelfWrap` exists (PR #4106), and it is for the `recipient: sent / self: failed` case only.

## Problem

The new `OutgoingDmRetryService` from #4124 enumerates these recipient-failed rows and logs a count, but does not act on them. They sit on the queue until the user manually re-sends, or until `retry_count` reaches `maxRetries` and they fall out of the retryable filter. The `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure` comment ("both wrap statuses remain retryable on the queue row") promises auto-retry that does not yet exist.

## Desired Outcome

Add a `DmRepository.recoverFullSend(rumorId)` primitive that re-runs the full `sendRumor` (recipient + self) for a stored row, persisting `direct_messages` on success and updating queue-row status by outcome — the same shape as `sendMessage`'s success and partial paths.

Wire the primitive into the `OutgoingDmRetryService` strategy table as the second entry: `recipient: failed` rows dispatch to `recoverFullSend`.

## Scope

- New `NIP17MessageService.publishFullSend` (or reuse `sendRumor` directly) for an already-built rumor — same integration shape as `publishSelfWrap` from PR #4106.
- New `DmRepository.recoverFullSend(rumorId)` that:
  - Looks up the row by id, validates ownership (mirror `recoverSelfWrap`'s account-scope check).
  - Rebuilds the rumor from `rumor_event_json`.
  - Calls `sendRumor` (or `publishFullSend`).
  - On success: runs the same `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` + atomic `direct_messages` insert that `sendMessage` does on its happy path.
  - On failure: marks both wraps `failed` and bumps retry — same shape as `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure`.
  - Idempotent: short-circuits if `recipientWrapStatus == sent` (a prior recovery already landed and the row has since been demoted to a self-wrap-only retry case — call `recoverSelfWrap` instead).
- Strategy-table wiring in `OutgoingDmRetryService` so `recipient: failed` rows are recovered the same way `recipient: sent / self: failed` rows are today.
- Tests pin: no double-publish to recipient if the prior attempt's recipient publish actually landed but local persistence failed; no duplicate `direct_messages` row inserted; sweep dispatches the right primitive per row state.

## Edge cases to design carefully

- **Recipient publish actually landed but local persistence failed last time.** The previous `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure` marks both wraps failed pessimistically — in this case, `recoverFullSend` would re-publish to the recipient. The receiver-side NIP-17 dedup keys on rumor id (preserved across retries via `rumor_event_json`) bound this to a duplicate gift wrap rather than a duplicate visible message, but it is still wasted bandwidth. Decide whether the design should query the relay for the rumor-id-tagged gift wrap before re-publishing.
- **App killed mid-publish (`pending: pending` rows).** Out of scope for #4124's `getRetryableForOwner` filter; covered by `getStillPendingForOwner` instead. Decide whether `recoverFullSend` covers both cases (state B and state C from the brainstorm) or whether state C gets its own primitive.

## Context

- Brainstorm that surfaced this gap: `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-10-issue4124-outgoing-dm-auto-sweep-brainstorm.md`.
- Production telemetry will come from #4124's enumeration log (`Log.info('OutgoingDmRetryService sweep complete: ... recipient-failed=N')`). Use those counts to prioritize this work.
- Sister issue #4127 covers Crashlytics surfacing for the doubly-degraded paths inside `recoverSelfWrap` and `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` — coordinate so this work does not duplicate that error-reporting decision.
- Parent epic: #3912 (DM reliability hardening).

issue.title: feat(dm): recoverFullSend primitive + auto-sweep wiring for recipient-failed DMs
issue.body:
## Description

Closes #4240. Final follow-up in the #3909 stack for the durable
outgoing-DM queue. With this change, `outgoing_dms` rows that finalize
as `recipient_wrap_status: failed` are auto-recovered by the
`OutgoingDmRetryService` foreground sweep instead of sitting idle on
the queue.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4240. Relates to #3909, epic #3912.

### What the gap looked like

`OutgoingDmRetryService` (PR #4241) shipped with a counting-only branch
for `recipient: failed` rows — the inline comment said `recovery
primitive lands in #4240`. Without that primitive, an app kill or
relay reject that finalized as recipient-failed left the row queued
indefinitely (only manual SnackBar retry, which mints a new rumor and
zombifies the original row, could recover).

### What this PR ships

Two commits, layered bottom-up:

**1. `feat(dm): add recoverFullSend primitive` — repository layer**

`DmRepository.recoverFullSend(rumorId)` mirrors `recoverSelfWrap`'s
shape:

- Validates ownership against `_userPubkey` (multi-account isolation).
- Idempotent: if `recipientWrapStatus == sent` already (concurrent
  recovery raced ahead, or the original partial-success path promoted
  the row), defers to `recoverSelfWrap` so the recipient wrap is
  never republished.
- Rebuilds the rumor from `rumor_event_json` (preserves receiver-side
  dedup key across retries — minting a fresh rumor would defeat it).
- Calls `_messageService.sendRumor`, then finalizes via the existing
  `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` / `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure`
  helpers.
- On full success: inserts `direct_messages` + upserts the
  conversation row + deletes the queue row inside one
  `runInTransaction` — same atomicity contract as `sendMessage`'s
  happy path.
- On partial success: keeps the row at `recipient: sent / self:
  failed` so the next sweep replays the missing self-wrap via
  `recoverSelfWrap`.
- On recipient failure: re-marks both wraps failed with the new error.

Re-publishing a rumor whose original wire copy actually landed is
safe at the protocol level: NIP-17 receiver-side dedup keys on the
rumor id, preserved verbatim through `rumor_event_json`.

**2. `feat(dm): wire recoverFullSend into OutgoingDmRetryService` — service layer**

Strategy table after this change:

| Row state                          | Recovery primitive    |
|------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| `recipient: sent / self: failed`   | `recoverSelfWrap`     |
| `recipient: failed`                | `recoverFullSend`     |
| `pending: pending`                 | not in retryable filter; deferred |

The dispatch reuses the existing per-row backoff, `_isSweeping`
re-entrancy guard, and the `StateError` / `ArgumentError` /
unexpected-throw error policy from the `recoverSelfWrap` branch.

Sweep summary log gains `full-send-recovered=N full-send-failed=N`,
replacing the now-acted-on `recipient-failed=N` line. The class doc
comment is updated to state both strategy entries.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

These came up during the design but are explicitly deferred:

- **Pending-row recovery.** `pending: pending` rows (true app-kill
  mid-publish, no finalize wrote) remain out of
  `getRetryableForOwner`'s filter and are not handled here. The DAO's
  `getStillPendingForOwner` is the read primitive for that path; the
  open design questions (queuedAt time-gate to avoid stealing
  in-flight sends, cold-start-only trigger, whether to reuse
  `recoverFullSend` or split) belong in their own issue. Will file
  under epic #3912.
- **Observability for `recoverFullSend`'s swallowed paths.** PR #4402
  is wiring the `DmRepositoryErrorReporter` port across the existing
  7 swallow sites; once that merges, adding the 1-2 new sites in
  `recoverFullSend` is a one-line follow-up. Out of this PR to avoid
  a coordination dependency.
- **Manual-retry zombie cleanup.** Today, tapping Retry on the
  `failed` SnackBar (#3908) dispatches `ConversationMessageSent`,
  which mints a fresh rumor and a fresh queue row, zombifying the
  original failed row until auto-sweep exhausts its retries. Routing
  that path through `recoverFullSend(rumorId)` on the existing row is
  the right cleanup but expands UX surface beyond #4240's scope —
  separate PR.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Verification

From `mobile/`:

- [x] `dart format` — no diffs.
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- [x] `flutter analyze packages/dm_repository` — clean.
- [x] `flutter test packages/dm_repository` — **232 / 232 passing**
  (10 new `recoverFullSend` tests).
- [x] `flutter test test/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service_test.dart`
  — **27 / 27 passing** (6 new tests + 1 reworked).
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/dm test/screens/inbox
  test/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service_test.dart` — **359 / 359
  passing** (no regressions in adjacent DM bloc / view tests).

### Pinning contracts added

- `recoverFullSend` never invokes `sendRumor` when `recipientWrapStatus
  == sent` (idempotent guard defers to `recoverSelfWrap`).
- `recoverFullSend` never inserts into `direct_messages` on recipient
  publish failure.
- Sweep dispatches `recoverFullSend` for `recipient: failed` rows.
- Sweep dispatches `recoverSelfWrap` for `recipient: sent / self:
  failed` rows.
- Sweep never invokes `sendMessage` / `sendGroupMessage` for any
  retryable row (would zombify the queue row by enqueueing a new id).
- `recoverFullSend` is never invoked for rows where `recipient: sent`
  (those route through `recoverSelfWrap`).

### Manual verification (please confirm during review)

- [ ] Force a recipient publish failure on a 1:1 send (e.g. block the
      first `publishEvent` round in a debug build). Row finalizes at
      `recipient: failed / self: failed`. Background then re-foreground
      the app → row is recovered automatically → `direct_messages` row
      appears → queue row deleted.
- [ ] Same scenario but with sustained relay reject → row exhausts
      retries (5 attempts with 2s → 5min backoff) → falls out of
      `getRetryableForOwner`.
- [ ] Cross-account safety: send from account A, switch to account B,
      foreground → A's failed row is **not** recovered while B is
      active.
- [ ] Partial-delivery recovery still works (#4106 + #4241
      regression): force a self-wrap-only failure → SnackBar offers
      Retry → next foreground also sweeps it via `recoverSelfWrap` if
      the user dismisses the SnackBar.

## Acceptance check for closing #3909

After this PR lands:

| AC                                                       | Status |
|----------------------------------------------------------|--------|
| 1. Survives app kill mid-send + auto-recovers           | ✅ for `recipient: failed`. Pending-row case deferred to follow-up. |
| 2. Partial-delivery visibly distinguished + recoverable | ✅ (#4106) |
| 3. #3908 tests stay green                                | ✅ |
| 4. New tests cover the matrix (DAO / repo / service)    | ✅ |
| 5. No regression in the SnackBar retry flow             | ✅ |

issue.title: epic(notifications): stabilize in-app notifications, unread state, and push delivery
issue.body:
## Summary
Notifications remain one of the highest-risk user-facing areas in the app. Active issues exist across unread-state correctness, row rendering, actor identity, tap-target routing, push registration reliability, and residual dual-system debt.

This issue is the coordination source of truth for notifications work this week.

## Assignee
`@Chardot`

## Weekly Priority
`P1`

## Weekly Priority Meaning
- `P1` means top priority for the week.
- `P2` means complete this week after P1 priorities are finished.

## Execution Order
1. unread/data correctness
2. tap-target/navigation correctness
3. row rendering / actor clarity
4. push registration and cold-start delivery
5. cleanup of dual systems / residual debt

## Subgroup
- `@Chardot` — DRI
- `@dcadenas` — push / auth-readiness / cold-start delivery
- `@realmeylisdev` — unread-state and notification data consistency
- `@untreu2` — routing / service-path bugs

## Coordination
The listed subgroup must review scope, sequencing, and ownership before implementation starts. Coordination may be synchronous or asynchronous. Do not wait for central coordination if the subgroup can resolve the question directly. Escalate only when blocked or when a product, design, or architecture decision is genuinely needed.

## Agent Execution Notes
Agents working from this issue must:
- treat this parent issue as the coordination source of truth for notifications
- read linked child issues before starting implementation
- follow the execution order unless explicitly told otherwise
- avoid narrow symptom-only fixes in known weak paths
- update linked issues if dependencies or scope change

## Engineering Standard
This work must not create new technical debt.

The expectation is:
- no temporary hacks, fragile stopgaps, or TODO-style deferrals without an explicit linked follow-up issue
- eliminate as much adjacent existing debt as possible while touching this area
- prefer fixes that move the codebase toward repository standards: explicit state-driven behavior, clear ownership boundaries, repository-appropriate abstractions, and test-backed changes
- if a short-term workaround is truly unavoidable, it must be called out explicitly in the issue and PR, with the follow-up issue linked before merge

Where relevant, use the audit issues created from PR `#3530` by `@omartinma` as the source of truth for debt repayment and refactor expectations in this area.

## Relevant Debt / Refactor Issues
- `#3596` Delete dual notification system
- `#3567` Fold legacy NotificationModel list-item into BLoC variant
- `#3590` Inconsistent error handling in notification methods
- `#3352` Replace readiness and notification polling timers with event-driven signals
- `#3656` Fix screens with missing error-state branches

## Scope
- in-app notification correctness
- unread badge/list/detail synchronization
- actor identity and row rendering
- navigation targets for likes/comments/replies/reposts
- push registration and cold-start reliability
- cleanup of legacy/duplicate notification paths

## Existing Related Work
- `#4015`
- `#4159`
- `#4048`
- `#4145`
- `#3387`
- `#4116`
- `#2845`
- `#3929`
- `#2337`
- `#3596`
- `#3567`
- `#3590`
- `#3352`
- PR `#4110`
- draft PR `#4162`

## Dependencies
- None

## Non-Goals
- unrelated inbox or DM feature work
- broad backend redesign beyond what is required to stabilize notifications
- generic UI polish outside notification surfaces

## Child Issues
- `fix(notifications): unify unread state across badge, inbox list, and detail open`
- `fix(notifications): complete tap-target routing for likes, comments, replies, and reposts`
- `fix(notifications): complete row styling, sizing, localization, and actor clarity`
- `fix(push): remove session-readiness races from FCM token registration and cold-start delivery`
- `refactor(notifications): remove dual notification system and finish bloc cleanup`

## Acceptance Criteria
- opening inbox always converges unread state correctly
- tapping any notification opens the correct destination
- actor display is correct for repost/reaction/comment variants
- push registration survives cold start and signed-in transitions
- no remaining split-brain unread logic between old and new notification paths

## Done When
- all P1 notification children are either complete or explicitly blocked
- the subgroup agrees the notification path is no longer carrying known avoidable debt introduced this week
- remaining debt is reduced, not increased


- `#4387` task(notifications): run post-fix regression sweep across unread, routing, dedupe, and push flows

issue.title: search: define canonical focus behavior across Explore and Search Results
issue.body:
## Summary

Search needs a defined and testable focus model across Explore and Search Results. Today, routing during partial input can cause keyboard/focus continuity to break.

Parent epic: #3801

## Agent Brief

This issue is about **focus and keyboard continuity**, not search quality.

Confirmed:
- Explore auto-navigates while the user is still typing.
- The destination search screen is created with a non-empty `initialQuery`.
- The destination field only auto-focuses when `initialQuery` is empty.
- Users have to manually bring the keyboard back.

## Confirmed facts

From code:
- `ExploreScreen._onSearchChanged()` pushes the search route on partial input.
- `SearchResultsAppBar` requests focus only when `initialQuery` is empty.

From issue history:
- #3020 already tracks the user-visible keyboard collapse symptom.

## Problem

We do not have a canonical search focus model. The current behavior is partly implicit and route-driven, which makes it hard to reason about and easy to regress.

## Questions to resolve

- If we navigate during typing, should focus transfer to the destination field automatically?
- If we require explicit submit to navigate, what should happen to focus before and after submit?
- Should keyboard continuity be guaranteed across all search entry points or only Explore?

## Acceptance criteria

- Search focus behavior is explicitly defined for Explore and Search Results.
- Keyboard continuity behavior is intentional and documented.
- The chosen behavior is covered by automated tests.
- #3020 can be resolved against this contract rather than ad hoc UI behavior.



---

## Assignee
`@NotThatKindOfDrLiz`

## Weekly Priority
`P1`

## Sequencing
- Resolve this before implementation children finalize.
- This is the UX-definition child under `#3801`.

Agents working from this issue must:

## Engineering Standard
Fix the problem without adding new technical debt. If the touched path already has known audit or refactor debt, repay the relevant portion as part of the implementation instead of layering on a narrow patch.

issue.title: search: audit result surfaces for blocklist / visibility consistency
issue.body:
## Summary

Search result surfaces need a consistent audit for blocklist, visibility, and filtering rules. We have prior fixes in this area, but they should be validated comprehensively instead of treated as one-off search bugs.

Parent epic: #3801

## Agent Brief

This issue is about **search result correctness across surfaces**.

Confirmed:
- We have at least one historical bug for blocked authors appearing in search results.
- A prior PR (#1204) fixed one path, but #948 remains open and should be reconciled.
- Search now spans people, videos, tags, and lists; correctness rules should be consistent.

Related issue:
- #948 — blocked author videos included in search results

## Problem

Search result filtering rules appear to have been fixed piecemeal. We need a unified audit so we know whether search respects blocklist and visibility rules across all result types and entry paths.

## Questions to resolve

- Which repositories/surfaces own blocklist enforcement for search?
- Are people/videos/tags/lists all applying the same visibility rules?
- Is #948 still genuinely open or is it a state-cleanup issue after #1204?

## Acceptance criteria

- Search result filtering rules are documented.
- All result surfaces are audited for blocklist / visibility consistency.
- Test coverage exists for the intended rules.
- #948 is either cleanly resolved or decomposed into any remaining concrete gaps.

issue.title: fix(push): send push control events to Divine relay with relay OK handling
issue.body:
## Summary

Push registration could look successful even when the Divine relay never accepted the event.
This change sends push registration, deregistration, and preference events directly to the configured Divine relay and waits for a relay OK response.
It also keeps the publish bounded so a late relay connection cannot write or queue a stale push-control event after the timeout.

## What Changed

Push control events now use the same targeted OK-confirmed publish path.
The relay layer now treats the caller timeout as one deadline for both sending and waiting for OK responses.
Same-URL fallback now distinguishes a failed send from a sent frame, and deadline-bound sends cannot queue stale EVENT messages.

- Route kinds 3079, 3080, and 3083 through `publishEventAwaitOk` with `targetRelays: [EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl]`.
- Let explicit target-relay OK publishes run even when the general relay pool has no connected relays.
- Skip the generic disconnected-relay retry when explicit target relays are provided.
- Bound `RelayPool.sendEventAwaitOk` with one deadline across `_sendCollect` plus OK waiting.
- Thread that deadline through `Relay.send`, `RelayBase.send`, and `WebSocketConnectionManager.sendJson`.
- Disable pending-message queueing for deadline-bound await-OK sends.
- Do not queue pending-auth messages for deadline-bound await-OK sends.
- Remove expired temp relays after deadline timeout so their connection waiters cannot flush stale control events.
- Track expected relays as soon as each send succeeds, so timeouts report the relays that actually received the frame.
- Avoid retrying a stalled same-URL normal target as a temp relay after the shared deadline is consumed.
- Allow same-URL temp fallback when the normal target path returns `false` immediately without sending.
- Log accepted, rejected, and no-response relay outcomes without logging encrypted push-control content.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4411

## Testing

I tested the push-control service paths, the client OK-publish wrapper, and the relay-pool timeout and fallback behavior.
I also verified the touched packages and the app analyzer after the SDK API change.

- `dart format packages/nostr_client/lib/src/nostr_client.dart packages/nostr_client/test/src/nostr_client_test.dart packages/nostr_sdk/lib/relay/relay_pool.dart packages/nostr_sdk/test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart`
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib/relay/relay.dart lib/relay/relay_base.dart lib/relay/relay_isolate.dart lib/relay/web_socket_connection_manager.dart lib/relay/relay_pool.dart test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart test/unit/relay_pool_auth_test.dart test/unit/relay_count_test.dart test/integration/relay_auth_test.dart test/integration/nip50_search_test.dart`
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed test/src/follow_repository_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/src/nostr_client_test.dart --plain-name "publishEventAwaitOk"`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart --plain-name "sendEventAwaitOk"`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart`
- `dart test test/unit/publish_outcome_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/services/push_notification_service_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/providers/push_notification_sync_test.dart`
- `dart analyze` in `mobile/packages/nostr_sdk`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile/packages/nostr_client`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile/packages/follow_repository`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile`
- `flutter test --no-pub` in `mobile`
- `git diff --check`

## Risks

The main behavior change is that explicit target publishes no longer wait for unrelated pool reconnects, and deadline-bound OK publishes no longer queue messages for later delivery.
That is intentional for push control events because a late queued control event can make the app report a failed publish while still mutating relay-side push state later.
The SDK `Relay.send` interface now accepts an optional deadline, so custom test relays and package-local fake relays were updated to match.

- A target URL already present in the normal relay pool is not retried as a temp relay after the normal path sends or queues the frame.
- A normal target path that returns `false` immediately can still fall back to a same-URL temp relay within the caller timeout.
- If the normal target path stalls until the shared deadline is exhausted, the publish fails fast instead of trying the same URL a second way.
- If a relay connects after the deadline, the deadline-aware send path returns false before writing the stale EVENT.
- This does not prove the push service processed the event after relay acceptance; it only confirms relay acceptance.

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

issue.title: perf(inbox): remove N+1 latest-message overlay queries in DmRepository
issue.body:
## Summary

Closes #4296 

PR #4286 introduced a correctness fix for stale inbox previews but created an N+1 read-path problem: every `watchAcceptedConversations` / `watchPotentialRequests` emission performed one `getMessagesForConversation(limit: 1)` query per conversation. This PR removes that fan-out while keeping the correctness guarantee.

## Changes

### Option A — batched overlay query (`db_client`)
`getLatestMessagesForConversations` was already added in the review feedback of #4286. `_overlayLatestMessages` now issues a **single** batched query per emit regardless of conversation count, down from N.

### Option B — write-path drift fix (`ConversationsDao`)
Root cause of the original staleness: `upsertConversation` used `insertOnConflictUpdate` which unconditionally overwrote `last_message_*` columns on every gift-wrap arrival, including older out-of-order ones during backfill.

`upsertConversation` now uses a conditional `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` that only updates the three last-message columns when the incoming `last_message_timestamp` is **strictly newer** than the stored value. A `forceUpdateLastMessage` parameter bypasses the guard for `_refreshConversationPreview` (post-deletion), where the replacement message is by definition the newest remaining one.

`current_user_has_sent` is also now a write-once ratchet at the SQL level (`false → true` only, never reversed).

The `DoUpdate.withExcluded` rewrite also makes the rest of the conflict contract explicit and typed: `subject`, `ownerPubkey`, and `dmProtocol` preserve the existing non-null value when an incoming upsert omits them, while incoming non-null values still overwrite; `createdAt` remains immutable after the row is first created.

### Transitional overlay
`_overlayLatestMessages` is kept as a read-path safety net for existing user databases that may have stale rows written before the write-path fix shipped. Removal is tracked in #4407 (requires a backfill migration).

## Tests

- **7 `ConversationsDao` tests**: out-of-order upsert does not overwrite a newer preview; in-order upsert does update; `forceUpdateLastMessage: true` bypasses the guard; `currentUserHasSent` is never flipped back to false; nullable conflict fields preserve existing values when omitted; nullable conflict fields overwrite when provided; `createdAt` stays immutable on conflict.
- **Existing overlay regression tests** from #4286 remain intact: overlay preview, re-sort by timestamp, file-message preview.
- Updated `dm_repository_test` stubs/verify calls to include the new `forceUpdateLastMessage` parameter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Inbox streams no longer perform one `getMessagesForConversation(limit: 1)` per conversation per emit
- [x] Inbox preview still shows true latest message even when the conversation row is stale
- [x] Ordering remains based on the real latest message timestamp
- [x] Existing regression coverage intact
- [x] Transitional code has a linked `TODO(perf4407)` pointing at #4407 with a clear removal plan
